_comment: Defaults for /audit. A project's .claude/audit/config.json is deep-merged
OVER this file, so a project only writes what is genuinely different.
Lists and strings REPLACE rather than merge — a project overriding
`exclude_paths` owns the whole list.
TWO EXCLUDE MECHANISMS, and the split is not cosmetic:
exclude_paths  literal directory prefixes, NO wildcards, passed to git
as `:(exclude)<path>`. Applies to lane file lists AND to
the symbol reference passes — this is for code that is
not ours at all (vendored, submoduled), whose tokens must
not count as references to our symbols.
exclude_re     an ERE matched against the path with `grep -v -E`, after
git has listed the files. Applies to lane file lists ONLY.
This is for our code that is outside audit scope (tests,
fixtures, type stubs) — references FROM those files still
have to be counted, or every test helper reads as dead.
Why not one mechanism: git's `:(exclude)` pathspec matches by extension
when the pattern carries a wildcard — `:(exclude)*.d.ts` drops every .ts
file in the repo, and `:(exclude,glob)**/*.d.ts` silently drops none
(verified on git 2.50). Positive pathspecs are exact; exclusions are not.
So anything with a wildcard in it belongs in exclude_re.
